# [Baseline] - WIN - U - Microsoft Outlook Cached Mode Off

Puts Outlook in Online mode and prohibits creating an OST file, so that no mailbox content lands on the device's disk.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | User (U) — assign to user groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| checkId | `INTUNE-BASE-161-UMicrosoftOutlookCachedModeOff` |
| Source | own baseline |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_U_Microsoft_Outlook_Cached_Mode_Off.json`](Baseline_WIN_U_Microsoft_Outlook_Cached_Mode_Off.json) |

> For a shared or kiosk device where the profile is not kept, and for those who do not want any mail content on disk. The price is high: without an OST, Outlook does not work offline, searching is a server query, and the user notices every hiccup in the connection. This variant does not belong on a laptop. Applies only to classic Outlook (the Win32 app from Microsoft 365 Apps); the new Outlook for Windows does not read these ADMX settings and has no OST. The well-known slider **amount of mail to keep offline** (3 months / 12 months / all, registry value `SyncWindowSetting`) is *not* in the settings catalog: the ingested `outlk16v2` ADMX has eighteen settings under *Cached Exchange Mode* and that slider is not one of them. Anyone who wants to set it can only do so via a custom ADMX import or the Office Cloud Policy Service — so outside this baseline.
